Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the UniBank Holdings Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Jordan Lee, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review UniBank Holdings's results for the third quarter. With me this morning are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Risk Officer; David Kim, Chief Credit Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Robert Hayes, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Jordan, and good morning, everyone. UniBank Holdings delivered exceptional results in the third quarter, exceeding expectations and demonstrating the strength of our diversified business model.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on accelerating revenue growth, improving profitability, managing risk effectively, investing in technology and innovation, enhancing customer experience, strengthening our brand, and delivering value to our shareholders.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights. Overall, we achieved transformative performance with record profits despite persistent inflation, Fed rate hikes, and geopolitical headwinds, driven by our Digital First, Customer Centric strategy. Fee income showed robust growth across wealth management, investment banking, and cards, fueled by market tailwinds and franchise expansion. Our efficiency ratio improved significantly, reflecting cost discipline and tech gains. Loan growth was solid across commercial, consumer, and mortgage segments, outpacing peers. We're advancing our capital return plans with higher dividends and aggressive buybacks. Net interest income trended strongly both year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter. Market conditions positively impacted non-interest income through diversified fees amid volatility.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning. UniBank Holdings reported net income of $2.1 billion for the third quarter, or $1.65 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 12.5% year-over-year and 2.7% quarter-over-quarter to $2.82 billion, driven by a 45 basis point expansion in net interest margin to 3.55% from 3.10% last year. Interest income surged 18.2% to $8.45 billion on higher yields across loans averaging $450 billion at 5.85% and securities at 4.20%, with 62% of loans variable-rate tied to SOFR and Prime. Interest expense rose 32.4% to $5.63 billion due to deposit betas at 65%, but we contained costs with average deposits steady at $520 billion. Sequentially, interest income grew 1.8% on $12 billion loan growth and securities optimization, realizing $150 million extra income. Regionally, U.S. NII rose 15% YoY with 3.72% NIM, Europe up 8% YoY but down 1% QoQ, and Asia-Pacific up 11% YoY and 5% QoQ. NIM peaked after five quarters of gains, with deposit betas stabilizing at 45% cumulative thanks to AI-driven pricing engines boosting core deposits 2% QoQ. We're focused on asset sensitivity with 75% floating-rate loans, $2 billion in swaps hedging cuts, deposit fortification via UniYield Select targeting $20 billion inflows, and de-risking CRE. For Q4, we guide $2.80 to $2.85 billion NII with NIM at 3.52% to 3.57%, assuming two Fed cuts.

Turning to non-interest income, it totaled $2.8 billion, up 12% year-over-year and 5% sequentially, now 28% of revenue. In CIB, investment banking fees hit $950 million, up 28% YoY and 18% QoQ, with $450 million in M&A advisory from deals like $15 billion tech mergers and $300 million DCM as issuers locked sub-5% yields, though HY spreads widened to 450 bps. Trading fell 8% YoY to $650 million on VIX at 15 compressing flows, with $75 million MTM losses on 10-year yields to 4.3%, equities steady at $250 million, and FX down 5%. Wealth and asset management grew 22% YoY to $750 million on $1.2 trillion AUM up 14%, $45 billion inflows, 30% higher performance fees in alternatives. Service charges and payments at $450 million up 5% YoY, cards $300 million up 10% on 12% volumes, treasury $50 million from RTP and FedNow. Americas up 18%, EMEA 2%, APAC 25%. We've invested $500 million in AI risk analytics improving VaR 25%, ESG fees doubled to $100 million, guiding mid-single digits Q4 growth.

Fee income specifically totaled $2.6 billion, up 14% YoY and 5% QoQ—our strongest since Q4 2021—now 28% of revenue, core up 12% excluding $50 million prior restructuring fees. Wealth management at $1.25 billion, up 18% YoY and 48% of fees, on $4.2 trillion AUM up 22% from $85 billion inflows and 12% market gains. Advisory/custody $650 million up 25% on $45 billion HNW mandates in alternatives with 15% U.S. share; brokerage $400 million up 12% on 20% volumes via UniWealth Platform with 15 million users post-First Republic integration; annuities $200 million up 10%. Americas +22%, EMEA +15%, APAC +25% with $350 billion AUM. AI Wealth Insights Engine boosted productivity 25%, cross-sell to 35%. Guide 12-15% FY24 growth targeting $100 billion inflows.

Investment banking $850 million up 9% YoY 20% QoQ, #2 M&A share, #3 ECM. Advisory $450 million up 15% on $200 billion volume including $35 billion Pfizer-like deals, sponsor rebound 25%; equity underwriting $250 million up 8% on $15 billion including $4.9 billion Arm IPO; DCM $150 million flat QoQ on 95 bps IG spreads, 30% HY loans. Americas 60% +12%, EMEA +25%, APAC +2%. IBX NextGen cut settlements 50%, prioritizing Magnificent Seven and infrastructure for $1 billion fees. Outlook 10-12% FY24.

Cards $500 million up 11% YoY, 19% of fees, on 8% volumes to 2.1 billion swipes, $85 ticket. Interchange $320 million up 13% on 25% premium penetration; annual/late $120 million up 9%, delinq 1.2%; cross-border $60 million up 15%. U.S. +10%, int'l +14%, EMEA +5%. Tokenized Rewards pilot 20% Gen Z uptake, 40% rewards to wealth. Guide 10-13% with BNPL.

Our efficiency ratio stood at 57.2%, down 210 bps YoY from 59.3% and 40 bps QoQ from 57.6%, ahead of 61% industry median, nearing JPM's 52.8%. Non-interest expenses $4.2 billion up 2% YoY but flat QoQ, $250 million savings from 15% branch consolidation, 28% shift to digital cutting costs 15%. Revenue up 8% YoY to $7.3 billion on 12% NII, NIM 3.45%; non-interest +5%. Temenos Transact on 70% retail cut processing 25%, AI ops with Palantir/Google automated 40% reconciliation saving $120 million, fraud models 98.5% accuracy curbing losses 18%. North America 55.8%, Europe 60.1%, APAC 58.9%. ROTE 11.8% up from 9.5%. Target 56.5% 2024, sub-55% 2026 with $1.5 billion tech, $400 million gen AI savings.

Loans grew 6.2% YoY to $285 billion, +1.8% QoQ, outpacing 4.5% industry. Commercial 52% at $148 billion +8.1% YoY +2.4% QoQ: C&I $92 billion +12% on capex reshoring; CRE $56 billion +3.2%, delinq 0.45%, NCO 12 bps via Phoenix platform. Southeast 11%, Texas 6%, Elite Tier cross-sell +15%. Consumer $78 billion +5.7% YoY +1.2% QoQ: auto $42 billion +9% FICO 725 yield 7.2%; cards $22 billion +4%; personal +3% via Upstart. Delinq 2.1%, West/Midwest strong. Mortgage $59 billion +1.9% YoY flat QoQ: originations $4.2 billion, HELOC $12 billion +14% yield 8.1%, 21-day closes. Sunbelt +4%. Guide 6-7% FY, TCE 11.2%.

On capital returns, CET1 12.8% above 11.5-12.0% target. Dividend up 10% to $0.48 quarterly, 14th increase, 8% CAGR since 2019, payout 38% of adj EPS. Target mid-single digits 2025 growth, ROTCE 13-14%. Buybacks $3.2 billion YTD of $6 billion auth at $48.50 avg, +$0.65 EPS, TBVPS $32.40 up 7%. Complete by mid-2025, refresh $4-5 billion annual. Prioritize M&A >15% ROCE like $1.2 billion Midwest deal. $500 million RWA optimization shaved 20 bps, NCO 22 bps. Returned $7.8 billion past 12 months, 85% NI. Guide $10 billion+ annually.

Our capital ratios remain strong, and we are well-positioned to support future growth.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring interest rate fluctuations, credit migration in commercial real estate especially office sectors, and geopolitical tensions impacting trade finance. We are taking proactive steps like stress-testing under +200 bps shocks with losses under 1%, AI-enhanced VaR modeling, and reducing CRE to 220 bps RWAs to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile.

David Kim:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains exceptionally strong with non-performing loans at 0.65% and net charge-offs at 28 basis points for the year. We are actively managing our loan portfolio with criticized loans under 2.5%, reserves covering delinquencies well, and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment. Specifically, the performance of our commercial loan portfolio has been strong, with pristine rates in C&I and controlled CRE upticks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation, including the launch of our AI-powered Wealth Insights Engine and Tokenized Rewards pilot, which have seen strong customer adoption with 25% productivity boosts, 20% Gen Z uptake, and efficiency gains like 50% faster settlements and 25% reduced processing times across Temenos Transact and IBX NextGen platforms.

Robert Hayes:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include core modernization on AWS cloud cutting IT costs 22%, robotic process automation for 40% back-office tasks, and branch footprint optimization shifting 28% transactions to digital, contributing to improved productivity, $250 million run-rate savings, and real-time payments via blockchain pilots handling $50 billion.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide further insights into the fee income outlook across your key pillars?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks, John. Absolutely. We're guiding 12-15% fee growth for FY24 assuming stable markets, with wealth targeting $100 billion annual inflows via expanded RIA custody, investment banking 10-12% contingent on M&A recovery, and cards 10-13% with BNPL upside. Our $5 billion tech program through 2025 supports 12-15% CAGR, outpacing peers through balanced regional growth and cross-sell synergies like 35% consumer-to-wealth funding.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
What are your plans for capital returns amid potential M&A opportunities?

Michael Chen:
Great question, Mike. Dividends remain first priority with mid-single digit growth into 2025, supported by ROTCE expansion to 13-14%. We'll complete the $6 billion buyback by mid-2025 and refresh with $4-5 billion annually, keeping CET1 above 12%. M&A will be opportunistic for >15% ROCE deals to bolster deposits, as with our recent acquisition, while our 250 bps buffer handles CRE or rate cut scenarios.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
How are you managing commercial real estate risks in the current environment?

Lisa Patel:
Thanks, Lisa. We're highly selective, with CRE at 1.2-3.2% growth, delinq up just 15 bps to 0.45% in multifamily/office, NCO 12 bps, and exposure 220 bps RWAs with 65% LTV cushions. AI underwriting via Phoenix integrates real-time valuations, caps urban multifamily, and stress-tests +200 bps shocks under 1% losses per CCAR. Pivoting to healthcare/tech while elite relationship bundling boosts retention to 92%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Can you discuss the performance of your consumer loan portfolio?

David Kim:
Sure, David. Consumer loans grew 5.7% YoY to $78 billion, led by 9% auto expansion to $42 billion at 725 FICO and 7.2% yields via dealer networks. Cards up 4% to $22 billion on co-brand growth, personal +3% with Upstart decisioning under 60 seconds. Delinq 2.1% in line with peers, losses 85 bps, prioritizing unsecured with Plaid affordability checks for NIM accretion as deposits reprice.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Sarah Thompson for any closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your interest in UniBank Holdings. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
